L87: # Recording installed projects【81†¶】
L88: 
L89: This document specifies a common format of recording information about Python 【82†projects】 installed in an environment. A common metadata format allows tools to query, manage or uninstall projects, regardless of how they were installed.
L90: Almost all information is optional. This allows tools outside the Python ecosystem, such as Linux package managers, to integrate with Python tooling as much as possible. For example, even if an installer cannot easily provide a list of installed files in a format specific to Python tooling, it should still record the name and version of the installed project.
L91: ## The .dist-info directory【83†¶】
L92: 
L93: Each project installed from a distribution must, in addition to files, install a “`.dist-info`” directory located alongside importable modules and packages (commonly, the `site-packages` directory).
L94: This directory is named as `{name}-{version}.dist-info`, with `name` and `version` fields corresponding to 【84†Core metadata specifications】. Both fields must be normalized (see the 【85†name normalization specification】 and the 【86†version normalization specification】), and replace dash (`-`) characters with underscore (`_`) characters, so the `.dist-info` directory always has exactly one dash (`-`) character in its stem, separating the `name` and `version` fields.
L95: Historically, tools have failed to replace dot characters or normalize case in the `name` field, or not perform normalization in the `version` field. Tools consuming `.dist-info` directories should expect those fields to be unnormalized, and treat them as equivalent to their normalized counterparts. New tools that write `.dist-info` directories MUST normalize both `name` and `version` fields using the rules described above, and existing tools are encouraged to start normalizing those fields.
L96: 
L97: Note
L98: The `.dist-info` directory’s name is formatted to unambiguously represent a distribution as a filesystem path. Tools presenting a distribution name to a user should avoid using the normalized name, and instead present the specified name (when needed prior to resolution to an installed package), or read the respective fields in Core Metadata, since values listed there are unescaped and accurately reflect the distribution.
L99: Libraries should provide API for such tools to consume, so tools can have access to the unnormalized name when displaying distribution information.
L100: This `.dist-info` directory may contain the following files, described in detail below:
L101: 
L102:   * `METADATA`: contains project metadata
L103: 
L104:   * `RECORD`: records the list of installed files.
L105: 
L106:   * `INSTALLER`: records the name of the tool used to install the project.
L107: 
L108:   * `entry_points.txt`: see 【87†Entry points specification】 for details
L109: 
L110:   * `direct_url.json`: see 【88†Recording the Direct URL Origin of installed distributions】 for details
L111: The `METADATA` file is mandatory. All other files may be omitted at the installing tool’s discretion. Additional installer-specific files may be present.
L112: 
L113: This `.dist-info/` directory may contain the following directories, described in detail below:
L114: 
L115:   * `licenses/`: contains license files.
L116: 
L117:   * `sboms/`: contains Software Bill-of-Materials files (SBOMs).
L118: 
L119: Note
L120: The 【89†Wheel distribution format】 specification describes additional files that may appear in the `.dist-info` directory of a 【90†Wheel】. Such files may be copied to the `.dist-info` directory of an installed project.
L121: 
L122: The previous versions of this specification also specified a `REQUESTED` file. This file is now considered a tool-specific extension, but may be standardized again in the future. See 【91†PEP 376†www.python.org】 for its original meaning.
L123: ## The METADATA file【92†¶】
L124: 
L125: The `METADATA` file contains metadata as described in the 【84†Core metadata specifications】 specification, version 1.1 or greater.
L126: 
L127: The `METADATA` file is mandatory. If it cannot be created, or if required core metadata is not available, installers must report an error and fail to install the project.
L128: ## The RECORD file【93†¶】
L129: 
L130: The `RECORD` file holds the list of installed files. It is a CSV file containing one record (line) per installed file.
L131: 
L132: The CSV dialect must be readable with the default `reader` of Python’s `csv` module:
L133: 
L134:   * field delimiter: `,` (comma),
L135: 
L136:   * quoting char: `"` (straight double quote),
L137: 
L138:   * line terminator: either `\r\n` or `\n`.
L139: 
L140: Each record is composed of three elements: the file’s path, the hash of the contents, and its size.
L141: The path may be either absolute, or relative to the directory containing the `.dist-info` directory (commonly, the `site-packages` directory). On Windows, directories may be separated either by forward- or backslashes (`/` or `\`).
L142: The hash is either an empty string or the name of a hash algorithm from 【94†`hashlib.algorithms_guaranteed`†docs.python.org】, followed by the equals character `=` and the digest of the file’s contents, encoded with the urlsafe-base64-nopad encoding (【95†`base64.urlsafe_b64encode(digest)`†docs.python.org】 with trailing `=` removed).
L143: 
L144: The size is either the empty string, or file’s size in bytes, as a base 10 integer.
L145: For any file, either or both of the hash and size fields may be left empty. Commonly, entries for `.pyc` files and the `RECORD` file itself have empty hash and size. For other files, leaving the information out is discouraged, as it prevents verifying the integrity of the installed project.
L146: If the `RECORD` file is present, it must list all installed files of the project, except `.pyc` files corresponding to `.py` files listed in `RECORD`, which are optional. Notably, the contents of the `.dist-info` directory (including the `RECORD` file itself) must be listed. Directories should not be listed.
L147: To completely uninstall a package, a tool needs to remove all files listed in `RECORD`, all `.pyc` files (of all optimization levels) corresponding to removed `.py` files, and any directories emptied by the uninstallation.
L148: Here is an example snippet of a possible `RECORD` file:
L149: 
L150:     /usr/bin/black,sha256=iFlOnL32lIa-RKk-MDihcbJ37wxmRbE4xk6eVYVTTeU,220
L151:     ../../../bin/blackd,sha256=lCadt4mcU-B67O1gkQVh7-vsKgLpx6ny1le34Jz6UVo,221
L152:     __pycache__/black.cpython-38.pyc,,
L153:     __pycache__/blackd.cpython-38.pyc,,
L154:     black-19.10b0.dist-info/INSTALLER,sha256=zuuue4knoyJ-UwPPXg8fezS7VCrXJQrAP7zeNuwvFQg,4
L155:     black-19.10b0.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE,sha256=nAQo8MO0d5hQz1vZbhGqqK_HLUqG1KNiI9erouWNbgA,1080
L156:     black-19.10b0.dist-info/METADATA,sha256=UN40nGoVVTSpvLrTBwNsXgZdZIwoKFSrrDDHP6B7-A0,58841
L157:     black-19.10b0.dist-info/RECORD,,
L158:     black.py,sha256=45IF72OgNfF8WpeNHnxV2QGfbCLubV5Xjl55cI65kYs,140161
L159:     blackd.py,sha256=JCxaK4hLkMRwVfZMj8FRpRRYC0172-juKqbN22bISLE,6672
L160:     blib2to3/__init__.py,sha256=9_8wL9Scv8_Cs8HJyJHGvx1vwXErsuvlsAqNZLcJQR0,8
L161:     blib2to3/__pycache__/__init__.cpython-38.pyc,,
L162:     blib2to3/__pycache__/pygram.cpython-38.pyc,sha256=zpXgX4FHDuoeIQKO_v0sRsB-RzQFsuoKoBYvraAdoJw,1512
L163:     blib2to3/__pycache__/pytree.cpython-38.pyc,sha256=LYLplXtG578ZjaFeoVuoX8rmxHn-BMAamCOsJMU1b9I,24910
L164:     blib2to3/pygram.py,sha256=mXpQPqHcamFwch0RkyJsb92Wd0kUP3TW7d-u9dWhCGY,2085
L165:     blib2to3/pytree.py,sha256=RWj3IL4U-Ljhkn4laN0C3p7IRdfvT3aIRjTV-x9hK1c,28530
L166: If the `RECORD` file is missing, tools that rely on `.dist-info` must not attempt to uninstall or upgrade the package. (This restriction does not apply to tools that rely on other sources of information, such as system package managers in Linux distros.)
L167: 
L168: Note
L169: It is strongly discouraged for an installed package to modify itself (e.g., store cache files under its namespace in `site-packages`). Changes inside `site-packages` should be left to specialized installer tools such as pip. If a package is nevertheless modified in this way, then the `RECORD` must be updated, otherwise uninstalling the package will leave unlisted files in place (possibly resulting in a zombie namespace package).
L170: ## The INSTALLER file【96†¶】
L171: 
L172: If present, `INSTALLER` is a single-line text file naming the tool used to install the project. If the installer is executable from the command line, `INSTALLER` should contain the command name. Otherwise, it should contain a printable ASCII string.
L173: 
L174: The file can be terminated by zero or more ASCII whitespace characters.
L175: 
L176: Here are examples of two possible `INSTALLER` files:
L177: 
L178:     pip
L179: 
L180: 
L181:     MegaCorp Cloud Install-O-Matic
L182: This value should be used for informational purposes only. For example, if a tool is asked to uninstall a project but finds no `RECORD` file, it may suggest that the tool named in `INSTALLER` may be able to do the uninstallation.
L183: ## The entry_points.txt file【97†¶】
L184: 
L185: This file MAY be created by installers to indicate when packages contain components intended for discovery and use by other code, including console scripts and other applications that the installer has made available for execution.
L186: 
L187: Its detailed specification is at 【87†Entry points specification】.
L188: ## The direct_url.json file【98†¶】
L189: 
L190: This file MUST be created by installers when installing a distribution from a requirement specifying a direct URL reference (including a VCS URL).
L191: 
L192: This file MUST NOT be created when installing a distribution from an other type of requirement (i.e. name plus version specifier).
L193: 
L194: Its detailed specification is at 【88†Recording the Direct URL Origin of installed distributions】.
L195: ## The `licenses/` subdirectory【99†¶】
L196: 
L197: If the metadata version is 2.4 or greater and one or more `License-File` fields is specified, the `.dist-info/` directory MUST contain a `licenses/` subdirectory which MUST contain the files listed in the `License-File` fields in the `METADATA` file at their respective paths relative to the `licenses/` directory. Any files in this directory MUST be copied from wheels by the install tools.
L198: ## The `sboms/` subdirectory【100†¶】
L199: 
L200: All files contained within the `.dist-info/sboms/` directory MUST be Software Bill-of-Materials (SBOM) files that describe software contained within the installed package. Any files in this directory MUST be copied from wheels by the install tools.
L201: ## Intentionally preventing changes to installed packages【101†¶】
L202: 
L203: In some cases (such as when needing to manage external dependencies in addition to Python ecosystem dependencies), it is desirable for a tool that installs packages into a Python environment to ensure that other tools are not used to uninstall or otherwise modify that installed package, as doing so may cause compatibility problems with the wider environment.
L204: 
L205: To achieve this, affected tools should take the following steps:
L206:   * Rename or remove the `RECORD` file to prevent changes via other tools (e.g. appending a suffix to create a non-standard `RECORD.tool` file if the tool itself needs the information, or omitting the file entirely if the package contents are tracked and managed via other means)
L207: 
L208:   * Write an `INSTALLER` file indicating the name of the tool that should be used to manage the package (this allows `RECORD`-aware tools to provide better error notices when asked to modify affected packages)
L209: Python runtime providers may also prevent inadvertent modification of platform provided packages by modifying the default Python package installation scheme to use a location other than that used by platform provided packages (while also ensuring both locations appear on the default Python import path).
L210: 
L211: In some circumstances, it may be desirable to block even installation of additional packages via Python-specific tools. For these cases refer to 【102†Externally Managed Environments】
L212: ## History【103†¶】
L213: 
L214:   * June 2009: The original version of this specification was approved through 【104†PEP 376†peps.python.org】. At the time, it was known as the Database of Installed Python Distributions.
L215: 
L216:   * March 2020: The specification of the `direct_url.json` file was approved through 【105†PEP 610†peps.python.org】. It is only mentioned on this page; see 【88†Recording the Direct URL Origin of installed distributions】 for the full definition.
L217:   * September 2020: Various amendments and clarifications were approved through 【106†PEP 627†peps.python.org】.
L218: 
L219:   * December 2024: The `.dist-info/licenses/` directory was specified through 【107†PEP 639†peps.python.org】.
